summary.text: Son of Sisyphus and king of Ephyra (Corinth); father of Bellerophon, and the link by which the craft of Sisyphus passes to the slayer of the Chimera.

story.text: He stands at the centre of the Corinthian pedigree that Glaucus of Lycia recites to Diomedes on the battlefield of Troy: there was a city Ephyre in the heart of Argos, and there dwelt Sisyphus, craftiest of men; Sisyphus begat Glaucus, and Glaucus begat peerless Bellerophon.

Apollodorus fills out the line Homer leaves bare: Glaucus, son of Sisyphus, had by Eurymede a son Bellerophon, who slew the fire-breathing Chimera — so the throne of Ephyra and the heroic blood pass through Glaucus from the trickster of Corinth to its greatest hero.
His own end is grim and told only by Hyginus: at the funeral games of Pelias his mares, maddened, tore Glaucus apart — the origin of the ghost-horse Taraxippos that frightened teams at the Isthmus.
